[1/4] Plan: make startup temp cleanup age-based so a running Harbor's fresh upload buffer or prepared ZIP is never deleted by a CLI import/second instance; failing-first tests, README/ADR-033

impact_assessment.why: PhotoStore.__init__ unlinks every .tmp_upload_* in .harbor/incoming and Downloads.clean unlinks every .zip in .harbor/downloads. A CLI import constructs a second HarborApp against the same library while the server is running, so its startup cleanup can delete the server's in-progress upload or a prepared download that has a live token
impact_assessment.benefits: Starting a CLI command or a second Harbor window no longer breaks an upload or download already in flight; only abandoned buffers older than the cleanup threshold are removed
impact_assessment.risks: contract: cleanup timing changes, not the paths or API; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: age check narrows the cross-process window without pretending to lock across processes; state: stale files may live up to the threshold instead of being deleted immediately
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use a six-hour age gate for uploads and a one-hour gate for downloads (their tokens expire in 15 minutes), test fresh versus stale buffers, keep unlink failures non-fatal, run the full suite and 4/4 gates, and record ADR-033

[1/4] Plan: validate profile password/key before any rename or insert, and answer 404 when a prepared ZIP vanished; failing-first HTTP/unit tests plus README/ADR-034

impact_assessment.why: ProfilesApi.update renames the person and their folder before validating a new password, and before the owner-key refusal, so a 400/403 request still renames them. ProfilesApi.create inserts the person before rejecting a bad password. Downloads.take returns a token for a ZIP that was deleted underneath it, which then fails with a 500 while serving
impact_assessment.benefits: A rejected write leaves no half-applied state; a vanished archive becomes a clear 404 and the token is dropped
impact_assessment.risks: contract: validation order and one missing-file response change; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: still no cross-process transaction, but no new partial state from validation; state: no schema change
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pre-validate password and owner-key rules before applying, keep the existing error messages, test that names/folders/profiles are unchanged after 400/403, test take() on a vanished ZIP, run the full suite and 4/4 gates, record ADR-034

[1/6] Retrospective push audit in expanding windows: last 3, 6, 9 ... all 80 pushes, newest to oldest; Run 1 (pushes 78-80) found case-only ZIP collisions, fix with failing-first test, ADR-035, then push

impact_assessment.why: The user asked for push-by-push verification in expanding windows; Run 1 covers pushes 78-80, including the ZIP entry-name counter added by push 79. Downloads._entry_name treats IMG.jpg and img.jpg as distinct, but Windows extraction is case-insensitive, so one photo can overwrite another in the delivered ZIP
impact_assessment.benefits: Downloads stay lossless on Windows and every later audit run starts from a proven baseline; each finding is attributed to its push range
impact_assessment.risks: contract: ZIP entry names can gain a hash suffix for case-only collisions; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: unchanged; state: no schema change
impact_assessment.mitigation: Casefold the used-name set, add a real two-photo ZIP regression, keep existing collision tests green, run 209+ tests and 4/4 gates, record ADR-035, commit and publish Run 1
